text:
maria: Quick check-in — pulling weekly spend vs commit for AcmeCorp. Yesterday shows a 38% spike in hosted API token usage vs target commit, auto-flagged as anomaly by billing-bot. Anyone actively troubleshooting? :thinking:

alex: saw the spike too. They shipped the new search-relevance A/B yesterday, likely heavier embeddings calls. I’ll ping the customer to confirm rollout timing.

sam: sharing the query I ran on the billing lake:
```
SELECT date, sum(tokens) as tokens, sum(cost_usd) as cost
FROM hosted_api_usage
WHERE customer_id = 'acme'
AND date >= '2024-05-01'
GROUP BY date
ORDER BY date DESC
LIMIT 14;
```
Results: last 3 days cost = [1.2k, 1.8k, 2.4k] USD. 7d avg vs commit shows +32%.

nisha: note their commit is $6k/mo with 10% burst allowance. If sustained, we risk overage charges — however they have a renewal conversation next week; we should be careful about surprise billing.

billing-bot: ALERT — spend variance >25% against commit for customer acme. Ticket created: #BILL-8937. Auto-tagged for CS and Finance.

maria: thanks. Action items: (1) alex to confirm A/B rollout and expected longevity, (2) sam to check error rate/latency during spike (maybe retries causing token inflation), (3) nisha to prepare overage projection and a mitigation note for renewal discussion. Please update this thread when you have answers.

alex: on it, will message their ENG lead and report back by EOD. :thumbsup:

sam: quick check — latency and 5xx% are flat, but client-side retries increased. I suspect SDK usage pattern change. I'll post a short snippet of suspicious call patterns shortly.

maria: if retries are client-side we should recommend a rate-limiting guide and the batching config from Redwood Optimize. @nisha can you prepare an estimated overage number for a 2-week sustained +25%?

nisha: will do. Quick calc: current commit monthly = $6k. +25% sustained => ~$7.5k/mo, pro-rated for 2 weeks ≈ $375. I'll put numbers in a one-pager.

alex: FYI — customer confirms the A/B will run for 3 days only. Likely spikes will subside, but I'll offer a temporary pulse-monitor and alert rule.

maria: perfect. If it looks like >48h sustained above 20%, we'll open a manual credit request and set a canary limit. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
